analysis:
Examined all three provider-release.md excerpts and the test-provider-ci-workflow.py metadata, changed ranges and bounded patch. The documentation change at docs/operations/provider-release.md:204–208 describes cold PR builds when a Sandbox lacks its dedicated cache; release workflows retain caching. It does not change release authorization, signing, qualification, publication or runtime serving permission. Surrounding documentation retains PR/master cache separation (201–225), exact signed-artifact provenance and publication checks (594–644), and revocation-preserving recovery (963–1068), relevant to A-005, A-011, A-017, T-013 and T-054. Shared model weights, APNs and memory limitations elsewhere in the excerpts are unchanged, not PR regressions. No supplied change demonstrates an encryption, tenant-cache isolation, billing or privileged-helper regression.
The visible test patch at scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py:152–168 adds expected rejection of restored .git links, hooks and executable/include configuration before repository validation. This is test evidence, not proof the build action implements those checks. Most of that file's changes have no supplied source, and its patch is truncated. Integration must inspect the actual cache-gating/build-action changes and complete tests: verify every cache operation is gated on cache availability for Sandbox PRs, release cache behavior stays intact, and restored Git state is rejected before executable Git features can run. Also reconcile caller-controlled conditions and PR/master cache scope with docs/operations/provider-release.md:201–208. These missing implementations materially limit the cache execution/provenance conclusion; no concrete regression is independently established here.
